title: Avocado Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Avocado Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Avocado nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and zinc in abukado, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Avocado nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your abukado (avocado) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, zinc, phosphorus, boron and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Avocado leaves with wide brown, scorched edges from potassium shortage

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, boron and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which avocado nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a avocado nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest avocado nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in avocado

At first the leaves just fade a little and new shoots grow more slowly. Later the dark green leaves turn evenly light green to yellow, the canopy thins out and new leaves are smaller, narrow and stiff. Trees set and hold fewer fruits. You see it most at this stage: young trees, and bearing trees after several years of fruiting with no fertilizer.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in abukado

Many Philippine avocado trees are grown with no fertilizer at all, which a review links to the fall in yield and quality after a few years of bearing. Heavy rain on sandy or eroded soils washes nitrogen away.
How to tell it apart

Phytophthora root rot also gives small, pale green or yellowish leaves and a thin canopy. But the leaves wilt even when the soil is wet, leaf tips brown, branches die back, and the small feeder roots are black, brittle and dead. To be sure, leaf test: pick leaves near the shoot tips from the last main flush, ones that have just finished growing and hardened, about 5 to 7 months old. Check roots and drainage.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Urea 46 0 0 in a ring under the canopy at the start and end of the rainy season. Philippine growers give young, non bearing trees 100 to 200 grams of Ammonium sulfate or 50 to 100 grams of Urea per tree twice a year. Bearing trees about 500 grams of Complete 14 14 14 twice a year. Full bearing trees about 2 kg of complete fertilizer a year. Add manure or compost.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in two splits and keep a mulch of leaves or compost under the canopy, away from the trunk.
Potassium deficiency in avocado

blocks.alt: Avocado leaves with wide brown, scorched edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Older leaves show it first. Yellowing starts between the veins and in an uneven band along the edge, then turns tan and brown. Scorched dead patches appear over the leaf. Leaves may curve downward. Fruits stay smaller, and Haifa notes the veins inside the fruit can turn black. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all while fruits fill.
Why potassium deficiency happens in abukado
Sandy or leached soils, heavy fruit crops, and fertilizer programs that give nitrogen only.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on old leaves, but the veins stay dark green and bright while the tissue between them pales. Root rot gives brown leaf tips too, but with wilting, a thin canopy and dead black roots. To be sure, leaf test of recently matured leaves near the shoot tips, 5 to 7 months old, and a soil test for potash.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Give bearing trees a fertilizer richer in potash, following the soil test. University of Florida advises mixes with 9 to 15 percent potash and only 2 to 4 percent phosphate for bearing trees. Add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 to the complete fertilizer in two splits during the rains.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, switch from a nitrogen only program to a complete fertilizer once trees bear, and return fallen leaves as mulch.
Zinc deficiency in avocado

Early on, the leaves yellow between the veins and come out a little smaller. In bad cases the leaves are much smaller and narrower, trough shaped and bent back, yellow or bronzed between the veins. Old leaves get many small dead spots. Twigs grow very short so the leaves crowd into tufts like a feather duster. Fruits stay small and round, sunburn easily and get dead spots on the skin, and twig tips die back. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, often worst while the crop matures and after long dry spells.
Why zinc deficiency happens in abukado
Limestone and high pH soils, long droughts without watering. Years of only chemical nitrogen with no manure or compost, as a Florida study found.
How to tell it apart

Iron deficiency also yellows young leaves between green veins, but the leaves keep their normal size and shape and do not tuft. Manganese deficiency starts as yellowing near the midrib that spreads out. To be sure, leaf test of recently matured leaves near the shoot tips, and a soil test for pH and zinc. Spray a few trees: small leaves that already formed only green up, but the next flush comes out normal size.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray Zinc sulfate with hydrated lime just before a main growth flush. In the Florida trial that cured little leaf, the mix was about 12 grams of Zinc sulfate and 6 grams of hydrated lime per liter of water for severe cases. Half that for mild ones. University of Florida advises 3 to 4 nutrient sprays a year with zinc for young trees.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give manure or compost along with chemical fertilizer, water in long dry spells, and keep zinc in the yearly foliar sprays.
Phosphorus deficiency in avocado

Signs are often not clear. Leaves look dull and can turn bronze, the veins on the underside turn purple, and leaf stalks may take a purple cast. Older leaves can show uneven dead spots between the veins. Growth is slow, the canopy is thin and leaves drop early. You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting, and trees on poor acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in abukado
Acid, weathered soils that lock up phosphorus and soils low in organic matter.
How to tell it apart

Potassium and magnesium deficiency also mark old leaves, but with yellowing between the veins rather than a dull purplish cast. Root rot also slows growth and thins the canopy, so check the roots. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test of recently matured leaves near the shoot tips.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Use a complete fertilizer for young trees, following the soil test. University of Florida advises mixes with 6 to 10 percent phosphate for young trees and 2 to 4 percent for bearing trees. Where the soil test is very low, add 16 20 0 or Superphosphate 0 20 0 in the ring, and lime very acid soils.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus and compost in the planting hole and use a complete fertilizer in the first years.
Boron deficiency in avocado

blocks.alt: Deformed, lumpy avocado fruits, possibly from boron shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The shoot tips discolor, young leaves burn and twist, and their veins split and turn corky. Twigs may swell. Haifa adds small holes between the veins with a pale ring around each. In bad cases dead patches on branches and the trunk. Fruits can be lumpy, curved or misshapen, with sunken corky patches. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in abukado
No avocado particular causes were found in the sources. In other tree crops such as coffee it comes with soils low in boron, heavy liming, heavy potash and long droughts.
How to tell it apart

Calcium deficiency also distorts young leaves with dead tips and uneven edges, but without split corky veins. Copper deficiency kills the growing tips after the internodes shorten, with dark green leaves. To be sure, leaf test of recently matured leaves near the shoot tips, and a soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

University of Florida includes boron in 3 to 4 nutrient sprays a year for young trees, and possibly later. No avocado particular rate was found, so use Solubor or Borax at the label rate and retest. Too much boron is toxic.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add organic matter, mulch and water in dry spells.
Iron deficiency in avocado

Young leaves turn yellow between the veins while narrow strips along the veins stay dark green. Later the veins yellow as well and the leaves may fall. Leaves keep a normal size and shape. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, on limestone soils and after waterlogging.
Why iron deficiency happens in abukado

Alkaline, high pH soils such as limestone soils, overliming, and waterlogged soils. University of Florida notes that wet, poorly drained soils bring on nutrient deficiency signs and dieback in avocado.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency also yellows young leaves between the veins, but the leaves are small, narrow and crowded in tufts. Manganese deficiency starts near the midrib and turns dull. To be sure, soil test for pH and check drainage. Look at the roots.
What to apply for iron deficiency

University of Florida advises iron chelate made for high pH soils, drenched into the soil under the canopy from late spring through summer, because foliar iron sprays are generally not effective on avocado. Its table gives about 15 to 20 grams of chelate per tree a year in the first year, rising to about 55 to 110 grams for trees five years and older. Improve drainage where water stands.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, plant on a mound where water stands, avoid overwatering and overliming.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any avocado nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your abukado needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Avocado nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my abukado leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: leaves fade from dark green to light green or yellow. Thin canopy of small leaves and few fruits. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in avocado?
items.a: Apply Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Urea 46 0 0 in a ring under the canopy at the start and end of the rainy season. Philippine growers give young, non bearing trees 100 to 200 grams of Ammonium sulfate or 50 to 100 grams of Urea per tree twice a year.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in avocado?
items.a: Give bearing trees a fertilizer richer in potash, following the soil test. University of Florida advises mixes with 9 to 15 percent potash and only 2 to 4 percent phosphate for bearing trees.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes zinc deficiency in avocado?
items.a: Spray Zinc sulfate with hydrated lime just before a main growth flush. In the Florida trial that cured little leaf, the mix was about 12 grams of Zinc sulfate and 6 grams of hydrated lime per liter of water for severe cases.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my abukado lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the avocado nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
